html:
Bal Gangadhar Tilak was the first leader of the Indian national movement to win a mass following. His slogan was "Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it". People called him Lokmanya, "honoured by the people".

He was a Brahmin from the Konkan coast, a mathematics teacher and Sanskrit scholar in Pune. In 1881 he started two newspapers, Kesari in Marathi and Mahratta in English, and used them to attack the government.

The early Indian National Congress sent polite petitions. Tilak wanted pressure from below. He turned the household worship of Ganesh into a public festival in 1893 and began a festival of Shivaji, both of which drew crowds to political speeches. Critics say this tied nationalism to Hindu feeling and left Muslims out.

He was jailed for sedition in 1897. After the partition of Bengal he led the "extremists" who called for boycott and self-rule, and Congress split in 1907. In 1908 he was sent to prison in Mandalay for six years, where he wrote a long study of the Bhagavad Gita as a call to action.

Freed, he founded a Home Rule League and made a pact with the Muslim League in 1916. He died on 1 August 1920, the day Gandhi's non-cooperation movement began.
sum: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was the first leader of the Indian national movement to win a mass following. His slogan was "Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it". People called him Lokmanya, "honoured by the people".
